1| # Termux-AI — Orion
2| 
3| A modular, self-correcting autonomous AI agent for Termux. Orion runs entirely on-device, uses free cloud LLM APIs for inference, and exposes a terminal chat loop with tool use, persistent memory, voice I/O, chunk-based context compression, and a full agentic execution layer.
4| 
5| ---
6| 
7| ## Features
8| 
9| - **Multi-provider LLM fallback** — Cycles through Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Groq, and NVIDIA models automatically. Rate-limited or invalid keys rotate to the next key for the same model; a transient server error (500/502/503/504) skips straight to the next model instead of retrying every key for it.
10| - **Tool use** — `run_code`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `web_scrape`, `save_memory`, `retrieve_memory`, `index_files`, `intermediate_print`, `sleep_mode`.
11| - **Enhanced Tool Suite** — 7 new utility tools added:
12|   - `search_in_files` - recursive file content search with advanced options and filters
13|   - `list_directory` - directory listing with configurable depth
14|   - `search_files` - filename pattern matching with wildcard support
15|   - `rename_file` - safe file/directory rename/move with protection
16|   - `delete_file` - secure file/directory deletion with safety checks
17|   - `http_request` - HTTP client for API calls with comprehensive headers
18|   - `get_datetime` - current time information in multiple formats
19| - **Tool call transparency** — every tool call prints a collapsed one-line status by default; `Ctrl+O` (or `/expand`) reveals the full command/path and complete output. See [Tool Call Display](#tool-call-display).
20| - **Chunk-based context memory** — Conversation history is divided into stable numbered chunks. Old chunks are progressively compressed (short → micro → one-line summary) in a background thread. Raw chunks are permanently stored and retrievable by ID via `retrieve_chunk` / `list_chunks` tool calls.
21| - **Persistent memory** — Two-tier RAG system: personal facts (`memories.txt`) and indexed code/docs (`indexed_memory.txt`).
22| - **Agentic execution** — `/agent` triggers a Supervisor → Worker → Critic loop. Tasks are planned via `agent/planner.py`, executed with one retry, and persisted across restarts through `data/state.json`.
23| - **Enhanced Agent Interface** — Persistent agent mode state with direct prompts via `/agent [prompt]` syntax, clean toggle commands (`/normal`, `/chat`), `/expand`/`/collapse` for tool-detail visibility, and improved history tracking.
24| - **Modern Terminal Rendering** — Enhanced CLI code block styling with open-right gutter design, cleaner borders, and improved terminal integration.
25| - **Orchestration** — `orchestration/` provides multi-process task delegation (`Manager` → `Worker`) over a `multiprocessing.Queue` IPC channel.
26| - **Self-correction** — `reflection/` logs every execution outcome and automatically retries failures via `attempt_correction()`.
27| - **Voice I/O** — Optional STT via [Termux-STT](https://github.com/opsonusdh/Termux-STT) and TTS via `edge-tts` + `mpv`.
28| - **WhatsApp integration** — Send/receive messages and enable busy mode via [Termux-WP](https://github.com/opsonusdh/Termux-WP).
29| - **Safe execution** — `permissions.py` validates every shell command before dispatch.
30| - **Autonomous mode (opt-in)** — `/autonomous on` bypasses the permission layer entirely; off by default. See [Autonomous Mode](#autonomous-mode).
31| - **Advanced LLM Client** — Enhanced model slot organization with agent-specific slots, advanced error handling for API failures, reasoning budget exhaustion management, native reasoning metadata preservation, and tool execution timeout tracking.
32| - **Notifications (opt-in)** — When `notify: true` in `config/config.json`, a system notification is sent via `termux-notification` after agent tasks complete (both inline `/agent [prompt]` and persistent agent mode).
33|

176| ## Configuration (config/config.json)
177| 
178| The following options are available in `config/config.json`:
179| 
180| | Key | Type | Default | Description |
181| |-----|------|---------|-------------|
182| | `stt_path` | string | `~/Termux-AI/Termux-STT` | Path to Termux-STT module |
183| | `tts_enabled` | boolean | `false` | Start with voice mode enabled |
184| | `use_groq` | boolean | `false` | Use Groq TTS (faster, requires internet) |
185| | `show_details` | boolean | `false` | Show expanded tool output by default |
186| | `autonomous` | boolean | `false` | Bypass permission layer (opt-in) |
187| | `notify` | boolean | `true` | Send system notification after agent tasks complete |

203| ## Agent Mode
204| 
205| ```
206| YOU > /agent          # run one step: resolve next task → worker → critic
207| YOU > /agent auto     # loop until no pending tasks or a failure
208| YOU > /agent [prompt] # direct agent prompt with custom instructions
209| YOU > /normal         # switch to standard chat mode
210| YOU > /chat           # switch to conversational mode
211| ```
212| 
213| Initialize a project and add tasks through normal chat — Orion uses the `initialize_project` and `add_subtask` tools. State persists in `data/state.json` and survives restarts.
214| 
215| ### Agent Notifications
216| 
217| When `notify: true` in `config/config.json`, a system notification is sent via `termux-notification` after:
218| - `/agent auto` completes its loop
219| - `/agent [prompt]` finishes an inline agent task
220| - Persistent agent mode (`/agent` mode) completes a task
221| 
222| The notification appears in the Android notification shade with title "Termux-AI Agent" and message "Agent task completed" (or "Agent auto task completed").
223| 
224| To disable: set `"notify": false` in `config/config.json`.
225|

228| ## Autonomous Mode
229| 
230| ```
231| YOU > /autonomous on       # bypass the permission layer entirely
232| YOU > /autonomous off      # restore normal permission gating (default)
233| YOU > /autonomous status   # check which mode is currently active
234| ```
235| 
236| While autonomous mode is on, `run_code` never asks for approval — not for writes into `core/`, not for commands on the forbidden list, nothing. It's **off by default**, and the setting persists in `config/config.json`. Turn it on only when you trust what you're about to have the agent do: there's no per-action confirmation left to catch a mistake once it's on.

240| ## Tool Call Display
241| 
242| Every tool call prints to the terminal as it runs. Collapsed (the default) gives a one-line status per call; `Ctrl+O` / `/expand` reveals the full command or path plus the complete output (see [Input Controls](#input-controls)).
243| 
244| Running code (`run_code`) — collapsed:
245| 
246| ```
247| [EXEC]
248| echo "step 1"
249| echo "step 2"
250| echo "step 3"
251| [TOOL DONE] (0.34s)
252| ```
253| 
254| only the first three lines of the command are shown, and expanded shows the rest plus the full output:
255| 
256| ```
257| [EXEC]
258| echo "step 1"
259| echo "step 2"
260| echo "step 3"
261| [OUTPUT]
262| step 1
263| step 2
264| step 3
265| [TOOL DONE] (0.34s)
266| ```
267| 
268| Editing a file (`write_file`) / reading one (`read_file`) — collapsed shows nothing but the bare tag:
269| 
270| ```
271| [EDITING FILE]
272| [TOOL DONE] (0.08s)
273| ```
274| 
275| expanded:
276| 
277| ```
278| [EDITING FILE] core/llm_client.py | mode: overwrite | lines: 10-25
279| [OUTPUT]
280| Wrote 16 lines to core/llm_client.py
281| [TOOL DONE] (0.08s)
282| ```
283| 
284| Every other tool follows the same shape — `[TOOL_NAME]` collapsed, `[TOOL_NAME] <key argument>` plus a full `[OUTPUT]` block expanded — and a failed call closes with `[TOOL ERROR] (Xs)` instead of `[TOOL DONE]`. This is presentation only: the model always receives the complete tool output regardless of what the terminal happens to be showing.

306| ## Context Memory
307| 
308| Every conversation turn is stored as a numbered chunk in `logs/chunks.jsonl`. The active context window always stays small:
309| 
310| ```
311| [system] Chunk 1: <one-line summary>
312| [system] Chunk 2: <micro summary>
313| [system] Chunk 3: <short summary>
314| [user / assistant / tool]  ← raw chunk N-1
315| [user / assistant / tool]  ← raw chunk N  (most recent)
316| ```
317| 
318| Older chunks are compressed progressively in a background thread. The model can call `list_chunks` and `retrieve_chunk` to pull full raw history when needed.

35| ## Before Touching Any File
36| 
37| Read the target file in full before making any modification. This is not optional and not limited to "coding tasks." It applies whenever you intend to write, edit, or delete any file.
38| 
39| **Why:** You cannot safely modify a file whose current state you don't know. Memory of what a file "probably contains" is not the same as seeing it. Files change between sessions. A write based on a stale mental model causes regressions that are hard to trace.
40| 
41| **Pre-edit Analysis:**
42| Before proposing any code change:
43| 1. **Full File Read:** Always read the *entire* target file to understand its current state, context, and existing patterns.
44| 2. **Dependency Check:** Identify all direct and indirect dependencies of the code you intend to modify. Consider how changes might impact other modules or components.
45| 3. **Exact Line Number Identification:** For targeted edits, pinpoint the precise line numbers where changes need to occur.
46| 4. **Related Files:** If the task involves a new feature or significant change, proactively identify other files (e.g., `paths.py`, `core/tools.py`, `core/llm_client.py`) that might require corresponding updates.
47| 
48| **Action-gated rule:** Before any `write_file`, `run_code` (that writes), or bash command that modifies a file — confirm you have read that file in the current session. If you haven't, read it first.
49| 
50| ---
51| 
52| ## Recognize the Operation Type Before Starting
53| 
54| Before writing a single line, identify whether this is:
55| 
56| - **A targeted change** — one specific location, one specific edit → read → edit → verify
57| - **A bulk transformation** — the same change in N places → read → write a script → run once → verify
58| - **Adding a new component** — new function, new tool, new wrapper → plan the full addition chain first
59| 
60| **The bulk rule:** If the same pattern needs to change in more than three places in a file, do not make three individual edits. Write a Python script or use `sed` to make all changes in one pass. It is faster, more consistent, and does not consume round trips.
61| 
62| ---
63| 
64| ## 1. Environment Constraints
65| 
66| The system runs **primarily in Termux/Android** with cross-platform compatibility for Linux, macOS, and Windows:
67| 
68| - **No global writable paths.** `/tmp`, `/var`, `/usr/local` are not reliably writable across all platforms. All paths must resolve through `paths.py` under the project root (`~/Termux-AI`).
69| - **IPC limitations.** Named pipes (FIFOs) and POSIX shared memory are restricted on Android. Use `multiprocessing.Queue` exclusively.
70| - **Resource pressure.** Keep threads minimal, always join subprocesses, and close file handles in `finally` blocks.
71| - **Cross-Platform Compatibility.** Never hardcode OS-specific commands without a platform check (`sys.platform == 'win32'`). For Termux, prefer `termux-*` commands via wrappers.
72| 
73| ---
74| 
75| ## 2. Module Boundaries
76| 
77| Every package has a strict responsibility. Crossing these boundaries causes regressions.
78| 
79| | Package | Responsibility | Import Pattern |
80| |:---|:---|:---|
81| | `core/` | LLM inference, tool dispatch, context management, chat loop | flat imports within core (`from tools import *`) |
82| | `agent/` | Task state, planning, execution, validation | `from agent import state_manager` |
83| | `orchestration/` | Multi-process delegation, IPC | `from orchestration import Manager, Worker` |
84| | `reflection/` | Execution logging, failure analysis, auto-retry | `from reflection import ReflectionLoop, attempt_correction` |
85| | `tools/` | Platform hardware API wrappers only (Termux API) | `from tools import wrapper_termux_battery_status` |
86| | `config/` | Secrets and runtime settings — no logic | read via `paths.API_KEYS_FILE`, `paths.CONFIG_FILE` |
87| | `data/` | Persistent state and schemas — no logic | read/write via `agent/state_manager.py` only |
88| 
89| ### Absolute Rules
90| 
91| - **Do not wrap or replace `ask_ai()` and do not change its public return contract.** A bug fix inside `ask_ai()` is allowed only when the current task specifically requires it and the affected code is read and tested; prefer helper functions and provider-specific logic outside the public contract.
92| - **Never write to `data/state.json` directly.** Use `agent/state_manager.save_state()`.
93| - **Never append chat turns to the session `history` list.** `context_manager.build_history()` serves full conversation history from chunks.
94| - **Never summarize inside tool execution or between LLM calls.** `maybe_summarize_async()` runs only after `close_chunk()`.
95| 
96| ---
97| 
98| ## 3. sys.path Bootstrap
99| 
100| Every module that imports across packages must bootstrap `sys.path` the same way — `core/` first, root second:
101| 
102| ```python
103| import os, sys
104| _CORE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
105| _ROOT = os.path.dirname(_CORE)
106| if _CORE not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, _CORE)
107| if _ROOT not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(1, _ROOT)
108| ```
109| 
110| This must appear **before** any project imports.
111| 
112| ---
113| 
114| ## 4. Centralized Path Resolution (`paths.py`)
115| 
116| `paths.py` is the **single source of truth** for every file path. Import it everywhere:
117| 
118| ```python
119| import paths
120| 
121| state_file    = paths.STATE_FILE
122| api_keys      = paths.API_KEYS_FILE
123| config_file   = paths.CONFIG_FILE
124| logs_dir      = paths.LOGS_DIR
125| ```
126| 
127| ---
128| 
129| ## 5. Error Handling & Defensive Programming
130| 
131| - **Never swallow exceptions silently.** No `except: pass` or `except Exception: pass` without at minimum a `print` or log entry.
132| - **Programmatic Exception Diagnosis:** Inspect errors programmatically.
133| - **Idempotence & Safety:** Every script or background logic block must be safe to execute multiple times.
134| - **Timeouts and Resource Limits:** When interacting with external systems or long-running operations, implement explicit timeouts.
135| 
136| ---
137| 
138| ## 6. Concurrency Rules
139| 
140| - **Main inference thread is single.** `ask_ai()` is synchronous.
141| - **Two background daemon threads permitted:** context summarizer (`maybe_summarize_async`) and reflection logger.
142| - **Thread-safe state access.** `context_manager.py` uses `_lock` around all reads/writes to shared state.
143| - **No shared mutable state between processes.** `orchestration/Manager` communicates exclusively through `multiprocessing.Queue`.
144| 
145| ---
146| 
147| ## 7. Adding a New LLM-Callable Tool
148| 
149| 1. Write the implementation function in `core/tools.py`
150| 2. Add the JSON schema to `TOOLS_DESCRIPTION` in `core/llm_client.py`
151| 3. Add the dispatch `lambda` to `_dispatch_tool()` in `core/llm_client.py`
152| 4. If the tool wraps a platform API: create wrapper first in `tools/`, call it from `core/tools.py`
153| 5. Run syntax check on all modified files
154| 6. Write a minimal dispatch test that calls `_dispatch_tool()` and asserts the return value
155| 
156| ---
157| 
158| ## 8. Testing & Verification
159| 
160| Every change **MUST** be verified:
161| 
162| ```bash
163| # Syntax compilation check
164| python3 -m py_compile <path_to_file>
165| 
166| # Import check
167| python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'core'); import tools; print('OK')"
168| ```
169| 
170| If any, **MUST** fix errors that are found.
171| 
172| ---
173| 
174| ## 9. Python 3.10+ Best Practices
175| 
176| - **Type Hints:** Use explicit typing and `X | Y` for Union types.
177| - **Pattern Matching:** Use `match ... case` statements where suitable.
178| - **Context Managers:** Always use `with` statements for resource management.

1| # Termux-AI — Orion
2| 
3| A modular, self-correcting autonomous AI agent for Termux. Orion runs entirely on-device, uses free cloud LLM APIs for inference, and exposes a terminal chat loop with tool use, persistent memory, voice I/O, chunk-based context compression, and a full agentic execution layer.
4| 
5| ---
6| 
7| ## Features
8| 
9| - **Multi-provider LLM fallback** — Cycles through Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Groq, and NVIDIA models automatically. Rate-limited or invalid keys rotate to the next key for the same model; a transient server error (500/502/503/504) skips straight to the next model instead of retrying every key for it.
10| - **Tool use** — `run_code`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `web_scrape`, `save_memory`, `retrieve_memory`, `index_files`, `intermediate_print`, `sleep_mode`.
11| - **Enhanced Tool Suite** — 7 new utility tools added:
12|   - `search_in_files` - recursive file content search with advanced options and filters
13|   - `list_directory` - directory listing with configurable depth
14|   - `search_files` - filename pattern matching with wildcard support
15|   - `rename_file` - safe file/directory rename/move with protection
16|   - `delete_file` - secure file/directory deletion with safety checks
17|   - `http_request` - HTTP client for API calls with comprehensive headers
18|   - `get_datetime` - current time information in multiple formats
19| - **Tool call transparency** — every tool call prints a collapsed one-line status by default; `Ctrl+O` (or `/expand`) reveals the full command/path and complete output. See [Tool Call Display](#tool-call-display).
20| - **Chunk-based context memory** — Conversation history is divided into stable numbered chunks. Old chunks are progressively compressed (short → micro → one-line summary) in a background thread. Raw chunks are permanently stored and retrievable by ID via `retrieve_chunk` / `list_chunks` tool calls.
21| - **Persistent memory** — Two-tier RAG system: personal facts (`memories.txt`) and indexed code/docs (`indexed_memory.txt`).
22| - **Agentic execution** — `/agent` triggers a Supervisor → Worker → Critic loop. Tasks are planned via `agent/planner.py`, executed with one retry, and persisted across restarts through `data/state.json`.
23| - **Enhanced Agent Interface** — Persistent agent mode state with direct prompts via `/agent [prompt]` syntax, clean toggle commands (`/normal`, `/chat`), `/expand`/`/collapse` for tool-detail visibility, and improved history tracking.
24| - **Modern Terminal Rendering** — Enhanced CLI code block styling with open-right gutter design, cleaner borders, and improved terminal integration.
25| - **Orchestration** — `orchestration/` provides multi-process task delegation (`Manager` → `Worker`) over a `multiprocessing.Queue` IPC channel.
26| - **Self-correction** — `reflection/` logs every execution outcome and automatically retries failures via `attempt_correction()`.
27| - **Voice I/O** — Optional STT via [Termux-STT](https://github.com/opsonusdh/Termux-STT) and TTS via `edge-tts` + `mpv`.
28| - **WhatsApp integration** — Send/receive messages and enable busy mode via [Termux-WP](https://github.com/opsonusdh/Termux-WP).
29| - **Safe execution** — `permissions.py` validates every shell command before dispatch.
30| - **Autonomous mode (opt-in)** — `/autonomous on` bypasses the permission layer entirely; off by default. See [Autonomous Mode](#autonomous-mode).
31| - **Advanced LLM Client** — Enhanced model slot organization with agent-specific slots, advanced error handling for API failures, reasoning budget exhaustion management, native reasoning metadata preservation, and tool execution timeout tracking.
32| - **Notifications (opt-in)** — When `notify: true` in `config/config.json`, a system notification is sent via `termux-notification` after agent tasks complete (both inline `/agent [prompt]` and persistent agent mode).

203| ## Agent Mode
204| 
205| ```
206| YOU > /agent          # run one step: resolve next task → worker → critic
207| YOU > /agent auto     # loop until no pending tasks or a failure
208| YOU > /agent [prompt] # direct agent prompt with custom instructions
209| YOU > /normal         # switch to standard chat mode
210| YOU > /chat           # switch to conversational mode
211| ```
212| 
213| Initialize a project and add tasks through normal chat — Orion uses the `initialize_project` and `add_subtask` tools. State persists in `data/state.json` and survives restarts.
214| 
215| ### Agent Notifications
216| 
217| When `notify: true` in `config/config.json`, a system notification is sent via `termux-notification` after:
218| - `/agent auto` completes its loop
219| - `/agent [prompt]` finishes an inline agent task
220| - Persistent agent mode (`/agent` mode) completes a task
221| 
222| The notification appears in the Android notification shade with title "Termux-AI Agent" and message "Agent task completed" (or "Agent auto task completed").
223| 
224| To disable: set `"notify": false` in `config/config.json`.

228| ## Autonomous Mode
229| 
230| ```
231| YOU > /autonomous on       # bypass the permission layer entirely
232| YOU > /autonomous off      # restore normal permission gating (default)
233| YOU > /autonomous status   # check which mode is currently active
234| ```
235| 
236| While autonomous mode is on, `run_code` never asks for approval — not for writes into `core/`, not for commands on the forbidden list, nothing. It's **off by default**, and the setting persists in `config/config.json`. Turn it on only when you trust what you're about to have the agent do: there's no per-action confirmation left to catch a mistake once it's on.

240| ## Tool Call Display
241| 
242| Every tool call prints to the terminal as it runs. Collapsed (the default) gives a one-line status per call; `Ctrl+O` / `/expand` reveals the full command or path plus the complete output (see [Input Controls](#input-controls)).
243| 
244| Running code (`run_code`) — collapsed:
245| 
246| ```
247| [EXEC]
248| echo "step 1"
249| echo "step 2"
250| echo "step 3"
251| [TOOL DONE] (0.34s)
252| ```
253| 
254| only the first three lines of the command are shown, and expanded shows the rest plus the full output:
255| 
256| ```
257| [EXEC]
258| echo "step 1"
259| echo "step 2"
260| echo "step 3"
261| [OUTPUT]
262| step 1
263| step 2
264| step 3
265| [TOOL DONE] (0.34s)
266| ```
267| 
268| Editing a file (`write_file`) / reading one (`read_file`) — collapsed shows nothing but the bare tag:
269| 
270| ```
271| [EDITING FILE]
272| [TOOL DONE] (0.08s)
273| ```
274| 
275| expanded:
276| 
277| ```
278| [EDITING FILE] core/llm_client.py | mode: overwrite | lines: 10-25
279| [OUTPUT]
280| Wrote 16 lines to core/llm_client.py
281| [TOOL DONE] (0.08s)
282| ```
283| 
284| Every other tool follows the same shape — `[TOOL_NAME]` collapsed, `[TOOL_NAME] <key argument>` plus a full `[OUTPUT]` block expanded — and a failed call closes with `[TOOL ERROR] (Xs)` instead of `[TOOL DONE]`. This is presentation only: the model always receives the complete tool output regardless of what the terminal happens to be showing.

123| 
124| ## Sys.path Convention
125| 
126| Every module sets up sys.path the same way — **core/ first, root second**:
127| 
128| ```python
129| _CORE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))   # wherever this file lives
130| _ROOT = os.path.dirname(_CORE)                        # project root
131| if _CORE not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, _CORE)
132| if _ROOT not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(1, _ROOT)
133| ```
134| 
135| This ensures:
136| - `import tools` → resolves to `core/tools.py` (not `tools/` package)
137| - `import paths` → resolves to `paths.py` at project root
138| - `from agent import state_manager` → resolves via root
139| - `from orchestration import Manager` → resolves via root
140| 
141| ---
142| 
143| ## Key Data Flows
144| 
145| ### Normal chat turn
146| ```
147| interface.py
148|   → cm.open_chunk(user_input)
149|   → cm.build_history()  → [summaries of old chunks] + [raw recent chunks]
150|   → ask_ai(prompt, history=...)
151|       → tools.build_memory_block()  → RAG on memories.txt / indexed_memory.txt
152|       → LLM call (Google / Nvidia / Groq)  →  tool loop  →  final reply
153|   → cm.close_chunk(reply)
154|   → cm.maybe_summarize_async()   ← background thread, post-reply only
155| ```
156| 
157| ### Agent step (/agent trigger)
158| ```
159| interface.py → llm_client.run_agent_step()
160|   Supervisor: state_manager  →  resolve next task (active_task_id → cursor → first pending)
161|   Worker:     ask_ai(worker_prompt)  →  persist worker_output
162|   Critic:     ask_ai(critic_prompt)  →  persist critic_output
163|   If FAILED and retry_count < 1:
164|     retry: ask_ai again  →  critic again  →  mark completed or failed
165|   state_manager.update_subtask(...)  →  _update_cursor_and_active_task(advance=True)
166| ```
167| 
168| ### Reflection + self-correction
169| ```
170| agent.executor.execute_plan(plan)
171|   → agent.validator.validate_execution(result)
172|   → reflection.ReflectionLoop.record(plan, result, success)
173| 
174| reflection.attempt_correction()
175|   → ReflectionLoop.latest_entry()
176|   → if result.validation == 'Failure':
177|       → agent.executor.execute_plan(plan)   ← re-runs
178| ## Commands & Controls
179| 
180| | Command | Behaviour |
181| |---------|-----------|
182| | `/autonomous on` | Enable autonomous mode (bypasses permission prompts for shell commands) |
183| | `/autonomous off` | Disable autonomous mode (restores interactive permission prompts) |
184| | `/expand` / `/collapse` | Toggle detailed tool/reasoning outputs in the terminal |
185| | `/agent` | Run one agent step (Supervisor → Worker → Critic, one task) |
186| | `/agent auto` | Run agent steps in a loop until no pending tasks or failure |
187|

89| _key_cursor: dict[tuple[str, str], int] = {}
90| _bad_keys: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
91| _bad_models: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
92| _account_restricted_until: dict[str, float] = {}
93| _rate_limited_until: dict[tuple[str, str, str], float] = {}
94| _transient_until: dict[tuple[str, str], float] = {}

96| _RATE_LIMIT_COOLDOWN = 30.0
97| _TRANSIENT_COOLDOWN = 5.0
98| _ACCOUNT_RESTRICTION_COOLDOWN = 300.0

101| def _next_key(
102|     provider_id: str,
103|     model_name: str,
104|     excluded_keys: set[str] | None = None,
105| ) -> str | None:
106|     keys = API_KEYS.get(provider_id, [])
107|     if not keys or (provider_id, model_name) in _bad_models:
108|         return None
109| 
110|     excluded_keys = excluded_keys or set()
111|     bad = _bad_keys.get(provider_id, set())
112| 
113|     cursor_key = (provider_id, model_name)
114|     idx = _key_cursor.get(cursor_key, 0) % len(keys)
115|     for offset in range(len(keys)):
116|         key = keys[(idx + offset) % len(keys)]
117|         if key in bad or key in excluded_keys:
118|             continue
119|         _key_cursor[cursor_key] = (keys.index(key) + 1) % len(keys)
120|         return key
121|     return None

124| def _available_key_count(provider_id: str, model_name: str) -> int:
125|     if (provider_id, model_name) in _bad_models:
126|         return 0
127|     if _account_restricted_until.get(provider_id, 0.0) > time.monotonic():
128|         return 0
129|     if _transient_until.get((provider_id, model_name), 0.0) > time.monotonic():
130|         return 0
131|     keys = API_KEYS.get(provider_id, [])
132|     bad = _bad_keys.get(provider_id, set())
133|     now = time.monotonic()
134|     return sum(
135|         1
136|         for key in keys
137|         if key not in bad
138|         and _rate_limited_until.get((provider_id, key, model_name), 0.0) <= now
139|     )

144|     _bad_keys.setdefault(provider_id, set()).add(key)

147| def _mark_account_restricted(provider_id: str) -> None:
148|     # Organization/account restrictions affect every key under this provider.
149|     _account_restricted_until[provider_id] = (
150|         time.monotonic() + _ACCOUNT_RESTRICTION_COOLDOWN
151|     )

154| def _mark_model_bad(provider_id: str, model_name: str) -> None:
155|     _bad_models.add((provider_id, model_name))

157| 
158| def _mark_rate_limited(provider_id: str, key: str, model_name: str) -> None:
159|     _rate_limited_until[(provider_id, key, model_name)] = (
160|         time.monotonic() + _RATE_LIMIT_COOLDOWN
161|     )

163| 
164| def _mark_transient(provider_id: str, model_name: str) -> None:
165|     # 5xx/server overload is normally provider+model scoped, not credential
166|     # scoped. Skip the remaining keys for this model instead of hammering the
167|     # same failing endpoint with every credential.
168|     _transient_until[(provider_id, model_name)] = (
169|         time.monotonic() + _TRANSIENT_COOLDOWN
170|     )
171| 
172| 
173| def _clear_expired_state() -> None:
174|     now = time.monotonic()
175|     for provider_id, until in list(_account_restricted_until.items()):
176|         if until <= now:
177|             _account_restricted_until.pop(provider_id, None)
178|     for store in (_rate_limited_until, _transient_until):
179|         for identity, until in list(store.items()):
180|             if until <= now:
181|                 store.pop(identity, None)
182| 
183| 
184| def _temporary_retry_delay() -> float | None:
185|     _clear_expired_state()
186|     now = time.monotonic()
187|     deadlines = [
188|         until
189|         for until in (*_rate_limited_until.values(), *_transient_until.values())
190|         if until > now
191|     ]
192|     if not deadlines:
193|         return None
194|     return max(0.0, min(deadlines) - now)

197| def _reset_provider(provider_id: str) -> None:
198|     # Compatibility helper: reset temporary provider state. Permanent failures
199|     # stay disabled, except account restrictions which are deliberately cooldown-based.
200|     _account_restricted_until.pop(provider_id, None)
201|     for key in list(_key_cursor):
202|         if key[0] == provider_id:
203|             _key_cursor.pop(key, None)
204|     for identity in list(_rate_limited_until):
205|         if identity[0] == provider_id:
206|             _rate_limited_until.pop(identity, None)
207|     for identity in list(_transient_until):
208|         if identity[0] == provider_id:
209|             _transient_until.pop(identity, None)

212| def _error_status(exc: Exception) -> int | None:
213|     status = getattr(exc, "status_code", None)
214|     if isinstance(status, int):
215|         return status
216|     response = getattr(exc, "response", None)
217|     status = getattr(response, "status_code", None)
218|     if isinstance(status, int):
219|         return status
220|     message = str(exc)
221|     for code in (400, 401, 403, 404, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504):
222|         if re.search(rf"\b{code}\b", message):
223|             return code
224|     return None
225| 
226| 
227| def _is_rate_limit(exc: Exception) -> bool:
228|     status = _error_status(exc)
229|     s = str(exc).lower()
230|     return status == 429 or any(
231|         x in s for x in ("resource_exhausted", "rate limit", "rate-limit", "too many requests")
232|     )
233| 
234| 
235| def _is_transient(exc: Exception) -> bool:
236|     status = _error_status(exc)
237|     s = str(exc).lower()
238|     return status in {500, 502, 503, 504} or any(
239|         x in s for x in ("temporarily unavailable", "server error", "overloaded", "unavailable")
240|     )
241| 
242| 
243| def _is_account_restriction(exc: Exception) -> bool:
244|     """Identify 400-level account/org restrictions that are not model errors."""
245|     status = _error_status(exc)
246|     if status != 400:
247|         return False
248|     s = str(exc).lower()
249|     return any(
250|         x in s
251|         for x in (
252|             "organization has been restricted",
253|             "organization is restricted",
254|             "organization has been suspended",
255|             "organization is suspended",
256|             "account has been restricted",
257|             "account is restricted",
258|             "account has been suspended",
259|             "account is suspended",
260|             "project has been disabled",
261|             "project is disabled",
262|         )
263|     )
264| 
265| 
266| def _is_context_error(exc: Exception) -> bool:
267|     """Identify request-size/context errors independently of HTTP status."""
268|     s = str(exc).lower()
269|     return any(
270|         x in s
271|         for x in (
272|             "context", "token_limit", "max_tokens", "exceed",
273|             "excluding", "window", "too many tokens", "prompt is too long",
274|         )
275|     )
276| 
277| 
278| def _is_invalid_request(exc: Exception) -> bool:
279|     """Identify recoverable 400/422 request-shape errors."""
280|     status = _error_status(exc)
281|     if status not in {400, 422}:
282|         return False
283|     if _is_account_restriction(exc) or _is_context_error(exc):
284|         return False
285|     s = str(exc).lower()
286|     return any(
287|         x in s
288|         for x in (
289|             "invalid request", "invalid parameter", "invalid value",
290|             "invalid argument", "malformed", "unsupported field",
291|             "all elements", "expected", "must be",
292|         )
293|     )

296| def _msg_to_dict(msg) -> dict:
297|     """Serialize an SDK message while preserving native reasoning metadata."""
298|     if isinstance(msg, dict):
299|         d = dict(msg)
300|     elif hasattr(msg, "model_dump"):
301|         try:
302|             d = msg.model_dump(exclude_none=True)
303|         except Exception:
304|             d = {"role": getattr(msg, "role", "assistant")}
305|     else:
306|         d = {"role": getattr(msg, "role", "assistant")}
307| 
308|     if not isinstance(msg, dict):
309|         content = getattr(msg, "content", None)
310|         reasoning = getattr(msg, "reasoning", None) or getattr(
311|             msg, "reasoning_content", None
312|         )
313|         reasoning_details = getattr(msg, "reasoning_details", None)
314| 
315|         if content is not None:
316|             d["content"] = content
317|         if reasoning:
318|             d["reasoning"] = reasoning
319|         if reasoning_details is not None:
320|             d["reasoning_details"] = reasoning_details
321| 
322|         tool_calls = getattr(msg, "tool_calls", None)
323|         if tool_calls:
324|             serialised = []
325|             for tc in tool_calls:
326|                 tc_dict = {
327|                     "id": tc.id,
328|                     "type": "function",
329|                     "function": {
330|                         "name": tc.function.name,
331|                         "arguments": tc.function.arguments,
332|                     },
333|                 }
334|                 extra = getattr(tc, "extra_content", None)
335|                 if extra is None and hasattr(tc, "model_extra"):
336|                     extra = (tc.model_extra or {}).get("extra_content")
337|                 if extra is not None:
338|                     if isinstance(extra, dict):
339|                         tc_dict["extra_content"] = extra
340|                     elif hasattr(extra, "model_dump"):
341|                         tc_dict["extra_content"] = extra.model_dump(exclude_none=True)
342|                     elif hasattr(extra, "__dict__"):
343|                         tc_dict["extra_content"] = extra.__dict__
344|                 serialised.append(tc_dict)
345|             d["tool_calls"] = serialised
346| 
347|     if "reasoning_details" not in d and hasattr(msg, "model_extra"):
348|         extra = getattr(msg, "model_extra", None) or {}
349|         if isinstance(extra, dict) and "reasoning_details" in extra:
350|             d["reasoning_details"] = extra["reasoning_details"]
351| 
352|     return d

397| 
398|         if "tool_calls" in m and m["tool_calls"]:
399|             new_tcs = []
400|             for i, tc in enumerate(m["tool_calls"]):

407|                 has_sig = (

418|                 new_tcs.append(clean_tc)

461| # Individual lines longer than this in a *collapsed* command preview get cut
462| # off — "first three lines" is meant to stay a brief preview even if one of
463| # those lines is itself huge (e.g. a minified one-liner). Expanded mode is
464| # never capped: that mode's whole point is to show everything.

468| def _tool_header_lines(name: str, args: dict, expanded: bool) -> list[str]:
469|     """Build the tag/preview line(s) printed before [OUTPUT]/[TOOL DONE] for
470|     one tool call. Presentation-layer only — never touches the tool's actual
471|     return value, only what gets echoed to the terminal.
472|     """
473|     tag = _TOOL_TAGS.get(name, name.upper())
474| 
475|     if name == "run_code":
476|         bash = str(args.get("bash", "") or "")
477|         lines = bash.splitlines() or [""]
478|         if expanded:
479|             body = bash
480|         else:
481|             preview_lines = lines[:3]
482|             preview_lines = [
483|                 (l if len(l) <= _COLLAPSED_LINE_CHAR_CAP else l[: _COLLAPSED_LINE_CHAR_CAP - 3] + "...")
484|                 for l in preview_lines
485|             ]
486|             body = "\n".join(preview_lines)
487|             if len(lines) > 3:
488|                 body += "\n..."
489|         return [f"[{tag}]", body]
490| 
491|     if name in ("write_file", "read_file"):
492|         if not expanded:
493|             return [f"[{tag}]"]
494|         path = args.get("path", "")
495|         seg_start = args.get("segment_start")
496|         seg_end = args.get("segment_end")
497|         unit = args.get("unit", "lines") or "lines"
498|         span = f"{seg_start}-{seg_end}" if (seg_start is not None or seg_end is not None) else "all"
499|         if name == "write_file":
500|             mode = args.get("mode", "overwrite")
501|             return [f"[{tag}] {path} | mode: {mode} | {unit}: {span}"]
502|         return [f"[{tag}] {path} | {unit}: {span}"]
503| 
504|     if name == "find_replace":
505|         if not expanded:
506|             return [f"[{tag}]"]
507|         path = args.get("path", "")
508|         find_text = args.get("find", "")
509|         segment_start = args.get("segment_start")
510|         segment_end = args.get("segment_end")
511|         # Show truncated find text in header
512|         find_preview = find_text[:80] + ("..." if len(find_text) > 80 else "")
513|         find_preview = find_preview.replace(chr(10), "\n")
514|         if segment_start is not None or segment_end is not None:
515|             seg_desc = f" lines {segment_start or 1}..{segment_end or "end"}"
516|             return [f"[{tag}] {path}{seg_desc} | find: {find_preview}"]
517|         return [f"[{tag}] {path} | find: {find_preview}"]
518|         return [f"[{tag}] {path} | find: {find_preview}"]
519| 
520|     # Every other tool: unchanged detail-picking, restructured into the same
521|     # tag(+detail)-then-OUTPUT-then-TOOL DONE shape as EXEC/EDITING FILE.
522|     if not expanded:
523|         return [f"[{tag}]"]
524|     detail = ""
525|     preferred = ("path", "bash", "query", "url", "to", "jid", "filename", "prompt")
526|     for key in preferred:
527|         value = args.get(key)
528|         if value not in (None, ""):
529|             detail = str(value)
530|             break
531|     return [f"[{tag}]{' ' + detail if detail else ''}"]

1747| def run_agent_step(voice: bool = False) -> str:
1748|     """Execute a single step of the agent: Supervisor -> Worker -> Critic loop."""
1749|     global _in_agent_mode
1750|     _in_agent_mode = True
1751|     try:
1752|         state = state_manager.load_state()
1753|         if not state or state.get("status") != "active":
1754|             return "No active project found."
1755| 
1756|         subtasks = state.get("subtasks", [])
1757|         goal = state.get("goal", "Unknown")
1758| 
1759|         task = None
1760|         active_id = state.get("active_task_id")
1761|         if active_id is not None:
1762|             task = next((t for t in subtasks if t["id"] == active_id and t["status"] in ("pending", "active")), None)
1763| 
1764|         if task is None:
1765|             cursor = state.get("cursor")
1766|             if cursor is not None:
1767|                 task = next((t for t in subtasks if t["id"] == cursor and t["status"] in ("pending", "active")), None)
1768| 
1769|         if task is None:
1770|             task = next((t for t in subtasks if t["status"] in ("pending", "active")), None)
1771| 
1772|         if task is None:
1773|             return "No pending or active subtasks found."
1774| 
1775|         task_id = task["id"]
1776|         desc    = task["description"]
1777|         retry_count = task.get("retry_count", 0)
1778| 
1779|         def _worker_call() -> str:
1780|             prompt = (
1781|                 f"AGENT WORKER MODE\nProject Goal: {goal}\n"
1782|                 f"Execute Subtask {task_id}: {desc}\n\n"
1783|                 "Complete the task using available tools. Be precise and thorough."
1784|             )
1785|             return ask_ai(prompt, voice=voice)
1786| 
1787|         def _critic_call(worker_reply: str) -> str:
1788|             prompt = (
1789|                 f"AGENT CRITIC MODE\nTask: {desc}\nWorker Output:\n{worker_reply}\n\n"
1790|                 "Verify if the task was completed correctly. "
1791|                 "Reply with exactly 'VERIFIED' or 'FAILED: <reason>'."
1792|             )
1793|             return ask_ai(prompt, voice=voice)
1794| 
1795|         state_manager.update_subtask(task_id, status="active",
1796|                                      notes=f"Execution attempt {retry_count + 1} started.")
1797|         worker_reply = _worker_call()
1798|         state_manager.update_subtask(task_id, worker_output=worker_reply)
1799| 
1800|         critic_reply = _critic_call(worker_reply)
1801|         state_manager.update_subtask(task_id, critic_output=critic_reply,
1802|                                      verification=critic_reply)
1803| 
1804|         if "VERIFIED" in critic_reply.upper():
1805|             # IMPORTANT:
1806|             # The LLM critic is advisory only.
1807|             # It cannot establish epistemic PROVEN state.
1808|             state_manager.update_subtask(
1809|                 task_id,
1810|                 status="completed",
1811|                 notes=(
1812|                     "Execution accepted; LLM critic advisory only. "
1813|                     "No epistemic proof established."
1814|                 ),
1815|                 verification="CRITIC_ADVISORY_ONLY",
1816|             )
1817|             return (
1818|                 f"Subtask {task_id} completed. "
1819|                 "Critic marked it VERIFIED as an advisory execution result; "
1820|                 "no epistemic proof was established."
1821|             )
1822| 
1823|         if retry_count >= 1:
1824|             state_manager.update_subtask(task_id, status="failed",
1825|                                          notes=f"Final failure after retry. {critic_reply}")
1826|             return f"Subtask {task_id} failed after retry."
1827| 
1828|         print(f"{YELLOW}[Agent] Critic rejected task {task_id}. Running retry...{RESET}")
1829|         state_manager.update_subtask(task_id, retry_count=1, status="active",
1830|                                      notes=f"Retry 1 triggered. Previous: {critic_reply}")
1831| 
1832|         retry_worker_reply = _worker_call()
1833|         state_manager.update_subtask(task_id, worker_output=retry_worker_reply)
1834| 
1835|         retry_critic_reply = _critic_call(retry_worker_reply)
1836|         state_manager.update_subtask(task_id, critic_output=retry_critic_reply,
1837|                                      verification=retry_critic_reply)
1838| 
1839|         if "VERIFIED" in retry_critic_reply.upper():
1840|             # Critic remains advisory after retry as well.
1841|             state_manager.update_subtask(
1842|                 task_id,
1843|                 status="completed",
1844|                 notes=(
1845|                     "Execution completed on retry; LLM critic advisory only. "
1846|                     "No epistemic proof established."
1847|                 ),
1848|                 verification="CRITIC_ADVISORY_ONLY",
1849|             )
1850|             return (
1851|                 f"Subtask {task_id} completed on retry. "
1852|                 "Critic verification is advisory only; "
1853|                 "no epistemic proof was established."
1854|             )
1855|         else:
1856|             state_manager.update_subtask(task_id, status="failed",
1857|                                          notes=f"Final failure after retry. {retry_critic_reply}")
1858|             return f"Subtask {task_id} failed after retry."
1859|     finally:
1860|         _in_agent_mode = False

1| # Orion Skill System
2| 
3| This directory is the authoritative instruction/skill system for Termux-AI. The system prompt is intentionally small: this index routes work, and the selected skills contain the detailed rules.
4| 
5| ## Precedence
6| 
7| 1. Current user request and runtime safety constraints.
8| 2. Mandatory core skill(s) selected below.
9| 3. Matching imported domain skill(s).
10| 4. Inference and remembered context are never stronger than current files or commands.
11| 
12| A skill is active only after its current `SKILL.md` has been read with the file tool in this session. A mention of a skill path does not count as a read.
13| 
14| ## Mandatory core routing
15| 
16| | Task surface | Read first | Add when relevant |
17| |---|---|---|
18| | Every task | `core/bootstrap` | `core/communication` |
19| | Coding/editing/refactoring/new tools | `core/coding` | `core/verification`, `core/reasoning` for diagnosis, `core/tool_efficiency` for bulk work |
20| | Runtime/import/tool failure | `core/troubleshooting` | `core/reasoning`, `core/verification` |
21| | Secrets/private data/external side effects | `core/security_and_privacy` | `core/capabilities` |
22| | History/context/continuation | `core/memory_and_context` | `core/reasoning` |
23| | Delegation/Supervisor/Worker/Critic/IPC | `core/orchestration_workflows` | `core/verification` |
24| | Git/release/config/template maintenance | `core/release_and_maintenance` | `core/verification`, `core/security_and_privacy` |
25| | Platform wrappers/packages/cross-platform behavior | `core/environment_and_tools` | `core/security_and_privacy` |
26| | Decision/ambiguity/autonomy | `core/decision_making` | `core/reasoning` |
27| | User-facing reports/style | `core/communication` | selected domain skill |
28| | WhatsApp/SMS/notifications | `core/whatsapp_and_notifications` | `core/security_and_privacy`, `core/capabilities` |
29| | External/integrated capability question | `core/capabilities` | selected domain skill |
30| 
31| ## Hard execution gate
32| 
33| For a source-changing task, do not call the first mutating tool until the required core `SKILL.md` files have been read in the current session. After any change, read `core/verification` and perform the required checks.
34| 
35| ## Imported domain skills
36| 
37| The 32 supplied skills below are preserved as imported domain modules. Their useful procedures are retained, but repository compatibility is bound by `core/capabilities`, safety by `core/security_and_privacy`, and execution/verification by the core skills.
38|

1| # Termux-AI — Orion
2| 
3| A modular, self-correcting autonomous AI agent for Termux. Orion runs entirely on-device, uses free cloud LLM APIs for inference, and exposes a terminal chat loop with tool use, persistent memory, voice I/O, chunk-based context compression, and a full agentic execution layer.
4| 
5| ---
6| 
7| ## Features
8| 
9| - **Multi-provider LLM fallback** — Cycles through Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Groq, and NVIDIA models automatically. Rate-limited or invalid keys rotate to the next key for the same model; a transient server error (500/502/503/504) skips straight to the next model instead of retrying every key for it.
10| - **Tool use** — `run_code`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `web_scrape`, `save_memory`, `retrieve_memory`, `index_files`, `intermediate_print`, `sleep_mode`.
11| - **Enhanced Tool Suite** — 7 new utility tools added:
12|   - `search_in_files` - recursive file content search with advanced options and filters
13|   - `list_directory` - directory listing with configurable depth
14|   - `search_files` - filename pattern matching with wildcard support
15|   - `rename_file` - safe file/directory rename/move with protection
16|   - `delete_file` - secure file/directory deletion with safety checks
17|   - `http_request` - HTTP client for API calls with comprehensive headers
18|   - `get_datetime` - current time information in multiple formats
19| - **Tool call transparency** — every tool call prints a collapsed one-line status by default; `Ctrl+O` (or `/expand`) reveals the full command/path and complete output. See [Tool Call Display](#tool-call-display).
20| - **Chunk-based context memory** — Conversation history is divided into stable numbered chunks. Old chunks are progressively compressed (short → micro → one-line summary) in a background thread. Raw chunks are permanently stored and retrievable by ID via `retrieve_chunk` / `list_chunks` tool calls.
21| - **Persistent memory** — Two-tier RAG system: personal facts (`memories.txt`) and indexed code/docs (`indexed_memory.txt`).
22| - **Agentic execution** — `/agent` triggers a Supervisor → Worker → Critic loop. Tasks are planned via `agent/planner.py`, executed with one retry, and persisted across restarts through `data/state.json`.
23| - **Enhanced Agent Interface** — Persistent agent mode state with direct prompts via `/agent [prompt]` syntax, clean toggle commands (`/normal`, `/chat`), `/expand`/`/collapse` for tool-detail visibility, and improved history tracking.
24| - **Modern Terminal Rendering** — Enhanced CLI code block styling with open-right gutter design, cleaner borders, and improved terminal integration.
25| - **Orchestration** — `orchestration/` provides multi-process task delegation (`Manager` → `Worker`) over a `multiprocessing.Queue` IPC channel.
26| - **Self-correction** — `reflection/` logs every execution outcome and automatically retries failures via `attempt_correction()`.
27| - **Voice I/O** — Optional STT via [Termux-STT](https://github.com/opsonusdh/Termux-STT) and TTS via `edge-tts` + `mpv`.
28| - **WhatsApp integration** — Send/receive messages and enable busy mode via [Termux-WP](https://github.com/opsonusdh/Termux-WP).
29| - **Safe execution** — `permissions.py` validates every shell command before dispatch.
30| - **Autonomous mode (opt-in)** — `/autonomous on` bypasses the permission layer entirely; off by default. See [Autonomous Mode](#autonomous-mode).
31| - **Advanced LLM Client** — Enhanced model slot organization with agent-specific slots, advanced error handling for API failures, reasoning budget exhaustion management, native reasoning metadata preservation, and tool execution timeout tracking.
32| - **Notifications (opt-in)** — When `notify: true` in `config/config.json`, a system notification is sent via `termux-notification` after agent tasks complete (both inline `/agent [prompt]` and persistent agent mode).

203| ## Agent Mode
204| 
205| ```
206| YOU > /agent          # run one step: resolve next task → worker → critic
207| YOU > /agent auto     # loop until no pending tasks or a failure
208| YOU > /agent [prompt] # direct agent prompt with custom instructions
209| YOU > /normal         # switch to standard chat mode
210| YOU > /chat           # switch to conversational mode
211| ```

213| Initialize a project and add tasks through normal chat — Orion uses the `initialize_project` and `add_subtask` tools. State persists in `data/state.json` and survives restarts.
214| 
215| ### Agent Notifications
216| 
217| When `notify: true` in `config/config.json`, a system notification is sent via `termux-notification` after:
218| - `/agent auto` completes its loop
219| - `/agent [prompt]` finishes an inline agent task
220| - Persistent agent mode (`/agent` mode) completes a task
221| 
222| The notification appears in the Android notification shade with title "Termux-AI Agent" and message "Agent task completed" (or "Agent auto task completed").
223| 
224| To disable: set `"notify": false` in `config/config.json`.

228| ## Autonomous Mode
229| 
230| ```
231| YOU > /autonomous on       # bypass the permission layer entirely
232| YOU > /autonomous off      # restore normal permission gating (default)
233| YOU > /autonomous status   # check which mode is currently active
234| ```
235| 
236| While autonomous mode is on, `run_code` never asks for approval — not for writes into `core/`, not for commands on the forbidden list, nothing. It's **off by default**, and the setting persists in `config/config.json`. Turn it on only when you trust what you're about to have the agent do: there's no per-action confirmation left to catch a mistake once it's on.

240| ## Tool Call Display
241| 
242| Every tool call prints to the terminal as it runs. Collapsed (the default) gives a one-line status per call; `Ctrl+O` / `/expand` reveals the full command or path plus the complete output (see [Input Controls](#input-controls)).
243| 
244| Running code (`run_code`) — collapsed:
245| 
246| ```
247| [EXEC]
248| echo "step 1"
249| echo "step 2"
250| echo "step 3"
251| [TOOL DONE] (0.34s)
252| ```
253| 
254| only the first three lines of the command are shown, and expanded shows the rest plus the full output:
255| 
256| ```
257| [EXEC]
258| echo "step 1"
259| echo "step 2"
260| echo "step 3"
261| [OUTPUT]
262| step 1
263| step 2
264| step 3
265| [TOOL DONE] (0.34s)
266| ```
267| 
268| Editing a file (`write_file`) / reading one (`read_file`) — collapsed shows nothing but the bare tag:
269| 
270| ```
271| [EDITING FILE]
272| [TOOL DONE] (0.08s)
273| ```
274| 
275| expanded:
276| 
277| ```
278| [EDITING FILE] core/llm_client.py | mode: overwrite | lines: 10-25
279| [OUTPUT]
280| Wrote 16 lines to core/llm_client.py
281| [TOOL DONE] (0.08s)
282| ```
283| 
284| Every other tool follows the same shape — `[TOOL_NAME]` collapsed, `[TOOL_NAME] <key argument>` plus a full `[OUTPUT]` block expanded — and a failed call closes with `[TOOL ERROR] (Xs)` instead of `[TOOL DONE]`. This is presentation only: the model always receives the complete tool output regardless of what the terminal happens to be showing.

306| ## Context Memory
307| 
308| Every conversation turn is stored as a numbered chunk in `logs/chunks.jsonl`. The active context window always stays small:
309| 
310| ```
311| [system] Chunk 1: <one-line summary>
312| [system] Chunk 2: <micro summary>
313| [system] Chunk 3: <short summary>
314| [user / assistant / tool]  ← raw chunk N-1
315| [user / assistant / tool]  ← raw chunk N  (most recent)
316| ```
317| 
318| Older chunks are compressed progressively in a background thread. The model can call `list_chunks` and `retrieve_chunk` to pull full raw history when needed.

124| ## Sys.path Convention
125| 
126| Every module sets up sys.path the same way — **core/ first, root second**:
127| 
128| ```python
129| _CORE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))   # wherever this file lives
130| _ROOT = os.path.dirname(_CORE)                        # project root
131| if _CORE not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, _CORE)
132| if _ROOT not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(1, _ROOT)
133| ```
134| 
135| This ensures:
136| - `import tools` → resolves to `core/tools.py` (not `tools/` package)
137| - `import paths` → resolves to `paths.py` at project root
138| - `from agent import state_manager` → resolves via root
139| - `from orchestration import Manager` → resolves via root
140|

142| 
143| ## Key Data Flows
144| 
145| ### Normal chat turn
146| ```
147| interface.py
148|   → cm.open_chunk(user_input)
149|   → cm.build_history()  → [summaries of old chunks] + [raw recent chunks]
150|   → ask_ai(prompt, history=...)
151|       → tools.build_memory_block()  → RAG on memories.txt / indexed_memory.txt
152|       → LLM call (Google / Nvidia / Groq)  →  tool loop  →  final reply
153|   → cm.close_chunk(reply)
154|   → cm.maybe_summarize_async()   ← background thread, post-reply only
155| ```
156| 
157| ### Agent step (/agent trigger)
158| ```
159| interface.py → llm_client.run_agent_step()
160|   Supervisor: state_manager  →  resolve next task (active_task_id → cursor → first pending)
161|   Worker:     ask_ai(worker_prompt)  →  persist worker_output
162|   Critic:     ask_ai(critic_prompt)  →  persist critic_output
163|   If FAILED and retry_count < 1:
164|     retry: ask_ai again  →  critic again  →  mark completed or failed
165|   state_manager.update_subtask(...)  →  _update_cursor_and_active_task(advance=True)
166| ```
167| 
168| ### Reflection + self-correction
169| ```
170| agent.executor.execute_plan(plan)
171|   → agent.validator.validate_execution(result)
172|   → reflection.ReflectionLoop.record(plan, result, success)
173| 
174| reflection.attempt_correction()
175|   → ReflectionLoop.latest_entry()
176|   → if result.validation == 'Failure':
177|       → agent.executor.execute_plan(plan)   ← re-runs
178| ## Commands & Controls
179| 
180| | Command | Behaviour |
181| |---------|-----------|
182| | `/autonomous on` | Enable autonomous mode (bypasses permission prompts for shell commands) |
183| | `/autonomous off` | Disable autonomous mode (restores interactive permission prompts) |
184| | `/expand` / `/collapse` | Toggle detailed tool/reasoning outputs in the terminal |
185| | `/agent` | Run one agent step (Supervisor → Worker → Critic, one task) |
186| | `/agent auto` | Run agent steps in a loop until no pending tasks or failure |

4| ---
5| 
6| ## Termux-AI integration contract
7| 
8| - This skill is part of the repository's authoritative operating system. Apply it with the selected domain skills, not as an optional suggestion.
9| - Use the current project files and the tools actually available to Orion. Never invent a connector, package, API, or filesystem capability.

11| - When this skill conflicts with a more specific task skill, follow the task-specific rule only where the conflict is explicit; preserve repository safety and verification rules.
12| 
13| # Coding Standards
14| 
15| This document defines the coding standards, architectural rules, and safety guidelines for the Orion/Termux-AI codebase. The rules here exist for specific reasons — understanding those reasons is more important than memorizing the rules.
16| 
17| ---
18| 
19| ## 0. Instruction-Read Gate
20| 
21| This manual is executable policy for coding tasks, not background documentation.
22| 
23| Before any source-changing action:
24| 1. Read `instructions/skills/core/coding/SKILL.md` in the current session with the file tool.
25| 2. Read any additional required manuals identified by `core/PROMPT.md`.
26| 3. Read every target file before editing it.
27| 4. Record the verified target files and applicable manuals in the task scratchpad when the task is multi-step.
28| 
29| If `coding.md` has not been read in the current session, do not write, delete, or run a mutating command.
30| 
31| This gate is intentionally redundant with the system prompt: the prompt selects the policy, while this manual states the policy itself so the rule remains available if the task is resumed or the prompt is compressed.
32| 
33| ---
34| 
35| ## Before Touching Any File
36| 
37| Read the target file in full before making any modification. This is not optional and not limited to "coding tasks." It applies whenever you intend to write, edit, or delete any file.
38| 
39| **Why:** You cannot safely modify a file whose current state you don't know. Memory of what a file "probably contains" is not the same as seeing it. Files change between sessions. A write based on a stale mental model causes regressions that are hard to trace.
40| 
41| **Pre-edit Analysis:**
42| Before proposing any code change:
43| 1. **Full File Read:** Always read the *entire* target file to understand its current state, context, and existing patterns.
44| 2. **Dependency Check:** Identify all direct and indirect dependencies of the code you intend to modify. Consider how changes might impact other modules or components.
45| 3. **Exact Line Number Identification:** For targeted edits, pinpoint the precise line numbers where changes need to occur.
46| 4. **Related Files:** If the task involves a new feature or significant change, proactively identify other files (e.g., `paths.py`, `core/tools.py`, `core/llm_client.py`) that might require corresponding updates.
47| 
48| **Action-gated rule:** Before any `write_file`, `run_code` (that writes), or bash command that modifies a file — confirm you have read that file in the current session. If you haven't, read it first.
49| 
50| ---
51| 
52| ## Recognize the Operation Type Before Starting
53| 
54| Before writing a single line, identify whether this is:
55| 
56| - **A targeted change** — one specific location, one specific edit → read → edit → verify
57| - **A bulk transformation** — the same change in N places → read → write a script → run once → verify
58| - **Adding a new component** — new function, new tool, new wrapper → plan the full addition chain first
59| 
60| **The bulk rule:** If the same pattern needs to change in more than three places in a file, do not make three individual edits. Write a Python script or use `sed` to make all changes in one pass. It is faster, more consistent, and does not consume round trips.
61| 
62| ---
63| 
64| ## 1. Environment Constraints
65| 
66| The system runs **primarily in Termux/Android** with cross-platform compatibility for Linux, macOS, and Windows:
67| 
68| - **No global writable paths.** `/tmp`, `/var`, `/usr/local` are not reliably writable across all platforms. All paths must resolve through `paths.py` under the project root (`~/Termux-AI`).
69| - **IPC limitations.** Named pipes (FIFOs) and POSIX shared memory are restricted on Android. Use `multiprocessing.Queue` exclusively.
70| - **Resource pressure.** Keep threads minimal, always join subprocesses, and close file handles in `finally` blocks.
71| - **Cross-Platform Compatibility.** Never hardcode OS-specific commands without a platform check (`sys.platform == 'win32'`). For Termux, prefer `termux-*` commands via wrappers.
72| 
73| ---
74| 
75| ## 2. Module Boundaries
76| 
77| Every package has a strict responsibility. Crossing these boundaries causes regressions.
78| 
79| | Package | Responsibility | Import Pattern |
80| |:---|:---|:---|
81| | `core/` | LLM inference, tool dispatch, context management, chat loop | flat imports within core (`from tools import *`) |
82| | `agent/` | Task state, planning, execution, validation | `from agent import state_manager` |
83| | `orchestration/` | Multi-process delegation, IPC | `from orchestration import Manager, Worker` |
84| | `reflection/` | Execution logging, failure analysis, auto-retry | `from reflection import ReflectionLoop, attempt_correction` |
85| | `tools/` | Platform hardware API wrappers only (Termux API) | `from tools import wrapper_termux_battery_status` |
86| | `config/` | Secrets and runtime settings — no logic | read via `paths.API_KEYS_FILE`, `paths.CONFIG_FILE` |
87| | `data/` | Persistent state and schemas — no logic | read/write via `agent/state_manager.py` only |
88| 
89| ### Absolute Rules
90| 
91| - **Do not wrap or replace `ask_ai()` and do not change its public return contract.** A bug fix inside `ask_ai()` is allowed only when the current task specifically requires it and the affected code is read and tested; prefer helper functions and provider-specific logic outside the public contract.
92| - **Never write to `data/state.json` directly.** Use `agent/state_manager.save_state()`.
93| - **Never append chat turns to the session `history` list.** `context_manager.build_history()` serves full conversation history from chunks.
94| - **Never summarize inside tool execution or between LLM calls.** `maybe_summarize_async()` runs only after `close_chunk()`.
95| 
96| ---
97| 
98| ## 3. sys.path Bootstrap
99| 
100| Every module that imports across packages must bootstrap `sys.path` the same way — `core/` first, root second:
101| 
102| ```python
103| import os, sys
104| _CORE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
105| _ROOT = os.path.dirname(_CORE)
106| if _CORE not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, _CORE)
107| if _ROOT not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(1, _ROOT)
108| ```
109| 
110| This must appear **before** any project imports.
111| 
112| ---
113| 
114| ## 4. Centralized Path Resolution (`paths.py`)
115| 
116| `paths.py` is the **single source of truth** for every file path. Import it everywhere:
117| 
118| ```python
119| import paths
120| 
121| state_file    = paths.STATE_FILE
122| api_keys      = paths.API_KEYS_FILE
123| config_file   = paths.CONFIG_FILE
124| logs_dir      = paths.LOGS_DIR
125| ```
126| 
127| ---
128| 
129| ## 5. Error Handling & Defensive Programming
130| 
131| - **Never swallow exceptions silently.** No `except: pass` or `except Exception: pass` without at minimum a `print` or log entry.
132| - **Programmatic Exception Diagnosis:** Inspect errors programmatically.
133| - **Idempotence & Safety:** Every script or background logic block must be safe to execute multiple times.
134| - **Timeouts and Resource Limits:** When interacting with external systems or long-running operations, implement explicit timeouts.
135| 
136| ---
137| 
138| ## 6. Concurrency Rules
139| 
140| - **Main inference thread is single.** `ask_ai()` is synchronous.
141| - **Two background daemon threads permitted:** context summarizer (`maybe_summarize_async`) and reflection logger.
142| - **Thread-safe state access.** `context_manager.py` uses `_lock` around all reads/writes to shared state.
143| - **No shared mutable state between processes.** `orchestration/Manager` communicates exclusively through `multiprocessing.Queue`.
144| 
145| ---
146| 
147| ## 7. Adding a New LLM-Callable Tool
148| 
149| 1. Write the implementation function in `core/tools.py`
150| 2. Add the JSON schema to `TOOLS_DESCRIPTION` in `core/llm_client.py`
151| 3. Add the dispatch `lambda` to `_dispatch_tool()` in `core/llm_client.py`
152| 4. If the tool wraps a platform API: create wrapper first in `tools/`, call it from `core/tools.py`
153| 5. Run syntax check on all modified files
154| 6. Write a minimal dispatch test that calls `_dispatch_tool()` and asserts the return value
155| 
156| ---
157| 
158| ## 8. Testing & Verification
159| 
160| Every change **MUST** be verified:
161| 
162| ```bash
163| # Syntax compilation check
164| python3 -m py_compile <path_to_file>
165| 
166| # Import check
167| python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'core'); import tools; print('OK')"
168| ```
169| 
170| If any, **MUST** fix errors that are found.
171| 
172| ---
173| 
174| ## 9. Python 3.10+ Best Practices
175| 
176| - **Type Hints:** Use explicit typing and `X | Y` for Union types.
177| - **Pattern Matching:** Use `match ... case` statements where suitable.
178| - **Context Managers:** Always use `with` statements for resource management.

1| # Termux-AI — Orion
2| 
3| A modular, self-correcting autonomous AI agent for Termux. Orion runs entirely on-device, uses free cloud LLM APIs for inference, and exposes a terminal chat loop with tool use, persistent memory, voice I/O, chunk-based context compression, and a full agentic execution layer.
4| 
5| ---
6| 
7| ## Features
8| 
9| - **Multi-provider LLM fallback** — Cycles through Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Groq, and NVIDIA models automatically. Rate-limited or invalid keys rotate to the next key for the same model; a transient server error (500/502/503/504) skips straight to the next model instead of retrying every key for it.
10| - **Tool use** — `run_code`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `web_scrape`, `save_memory`, `retrieve_memory`, `index_files`, `intermediate_print`, `sleep_mode`.
11| - **Enhanced Tool Suite** — 7 new utility tools added:
12|   - `search_in_files` - recursive file content search with advanced options and filters
13|   - `list_directory` - directory listing with configurable depth
14|   - `search_files` - filename pattern matching with wildcard support
15|   - `rename_file` - safe file/directory rename/move with protection
16|   - `delete_file` - secure file/directory deletion with safety checks
17|   - `http_request` - HTTP client for API calls with comprehensive headers
18|   - `get_datetime` - current time information in multiple formats
19| - **Tool call transparency** — every tool call prints a collapsed one-line status by default; `Ctrl+O` (or `/expand`) reveals the full command/path and complete output. See [Tool Call Display](#tool-call-display).
20| - **Chunk-based context memory** — Conversation history is divided into stable numbered chunks. Old chunks are progressively compressed (short → micro → one-line summary) in a background thread. Raw chunks are permanently stored and retrievable by ID via `retrieve_chunk` / `list_chunks` tool calls.
21| - **Persistent memory** — Two-tier RAG system: personal facts (`memories.txt`) and indexed code/docs (`indexed_memory.txt`).
22| - **Agentic execution** — `/agent` triggers a Supervisor → Worker → Critic loop. Tasks are planned via `agent/planner.py`, executed with one retry, and persisted across restarts through `data/state.json`.
23| - **Enhanced Agent Interface** — Persistent agent mode state with direct prompts via `/agent [prompt]` syntax, clean toggle commands (`/normal`, `/chat`), `/expand`/`/collapse` for tool-detail visibility, and improved history tracking.
24| - **Modern Terminal Rendering** — Enhanced CLI code block styling with open-right gutter design, cleaner borders, and improved terminal integration.

Raw chunks are permanently stored and retrievable by ID via `retrieve_chunk` / `list_chunks` tool calls.

203| ## Agent Mode
204| 
205| ```
206| YOU > /agent          # run one step: resolve next task → worker → critic
207| YOU > /agent auto     # loop until no pending tasks or a failure
208| YOU > /agent [prompt] # direct agent prompt with custom instructions
209| YOU > /normal         # switch to standard chat mode
210| YOU > /chat           # switch to conversational mode
211| ```
212| 
213| Initialize a project and add tasks through normal chat — Orion uses the `initialize_project` and `add_subtask` tools. State persists in `data/state.json` and survives restarts.
214| 
215| ### Agent Notifications
216| 
217| When `notify: true` in `config/config.json`, a system notification is sent via `termux-notification` after:
218| - `/agent auto` completes its loop
219| - `/agent [prompt]` finishes an inline agent task
220| - Persistent agent mode (`/agent` mode) completes a task
221| 
222| The notification appears in the Android notification shade with title "Termux-AI Agent" and message "Agent task completed" (or "Agent auto task completed").
223| 
224| To disable: set `"notify": false` in `config/config.json`.
225|

227| 
228| ## Autonomous Mode
229| 
230| ```
231| YOU > /autonomous on       # bypass the permission layer entirely
232| YOU > /autonomous off      # restore normal permission gating (default)
233| YOU > /autonomous status   # check which mode is currently active
234| ```
235| 
236| While autonomous mode is on, `run_code` never asks for approval — not for writes into `core/`, not for commands on the forbidden list, nothing. It's **off by default**, and the setting persists in `config/config.json`. Turn it on only when you trust what you're about to have the agent do: there's no per-action confirmation left to catch a mistake once it's on.

13| # Coding Standards
14| 
15| This document defines the coding standards, architectural rules, and safety guidelines for the Orion/Termux-AI codebase. The rules here exist for specific reasons — understanding those reasons is more important than memorizing the rules.
16| 
17| ---
18| 
19| ## 0. Instruction-Read Gate
20| 
21| This manual is executable policy for coding tasks, not background documentation.
22| 
23| Before any source-changing action:
24| 1. Read `instructions/skills/core/coding/SKILL.md` in the current session with the file tool.
25| 2. Read any additional required manuals identified by `core/PROMPT.md`.
26| 3. Read every target file before editing it.
27| 4. Record the verified target files and applicable manuals in the task scratchpad when the task is multi-step.
28| 
29| If `coding.md` has not been read in the current session, do not write, delete, or run a mutating command.
30| 
31| This gate is intentionally redundant with the system prompt: the prompt selects the policy, while this manual states the policy itself so the rule remains available if the task is resumed or the prompt is compressed.
32| 
33| ---
34| 
35| ## Before Touching Any File
36| 
37| Read the target file in full before making any modification. This is not optional and not limited to "coding tasks." It applies whenever you intend to write, edit, or delete any file.
38| 
39| **Why:** You cannot safely modify a file whose current state you don't know. Memory of what a file "probably contains" is not the same as seeing it. Files change between sessions. A write based on a stale mental model causes regressions that are hard to trace.
40| 
41| **Pre-edit Analysis:**
42| Before proposing any code change:
43| 1. **Full File Read:** Always read the *entire* target file to understand its current state, context, and existing patterns.
44| 2. **Dependency Check:** Identify all direct and indirect dependencies of the code you intend to modify. Consider how changes might impact other modules or components.
45| 3. **Exact Line Number Identification:** For targeted edits, pinpoint the precise line numbers where changes need to occur.
46| 4. **Related Files:** If the task involves a new feature or significant change, proactively identify other files (e.g., `paths.py`, `core/tools.py`, `core/llm_client.py`) that might require corresponding updates.
47| 
48| **Action-gated rule:** Before any `write_file`, `run_code` (that writes), or bash command that modifies a file — confirm you have read that file in the current session. If you haven't, read it first.
49| 
50| ---
51| 
52| ## Recognize the Operation Type Before Starting
53| 
54| Before writing a single line, identify whether this is:
55| 
56| - **A targeted change** — one specific location, one specific edit → read → edit → verify
57| - **A bulk transformation** — the same change in N places → read → write a script → run once → verify
58| - **Adding a new component** — new function, new tool, new wrapper → plan the full addition chain first
59| 
60| **The bulk rule:** If the same pattern needs to change in more than three places in a file, do not make three individual edits. Write a Python script or use `sed` to make all changes in one pass. It is faster, more consistent, and does not consume round trips.
61|

63| 
64| ## 1. Environment Constraints
65| 
66| The system runs **primarily in Termux/Android** with cross-platform compatibility for Linux, macOS, and Windows:
67| 
68| - **No global writable paths.** `/tmp`, `/var`, `/usr/local` are not reliably writable across all platforms. All paths must resolve through `paths.py` under the project root (`~/Termux-AI`).
69| - **IPC limitations.** Named pipes (FIFOs) and POSIX shared memory are restricted on Android. Use `multiprocessing.Queue` exclusively.
70| - **Resource pressure.** Keep threads minimal, always join subprocesses, and close file handles in `finally` blocks.
71| - **Cross-Platform Compatibility.** Never hardcode OS-specific commands without a platform check (`sys.platform == 'win32'`). For Termux, prefer `termux-*` commands via wrappers.
72| 
73| ---
74| 
75| ## 2. Module Boundaries
76| 
77| Every package has a strict responsibility. Crossing these boundaries causes regressions.
78| 
79| | Package | Responsibility | Import Pattern |
80| |:---|:---|:---|
81| | `core/` | LLM inference, tool dispatch, context management, chat loop | flat imports within core (`from tools import *`) |
82| | `agent/` | Task state, planning, execution, validation | `from agent import state_manager` |
83| | `orchestration/` | Multi-process delegation, IPC | `from orchestration import Manager, Worker` |
84| | `reflection/` | Execution logging, failure analysis, auto-retry | `from reflection import ReflectionLoop, attempt_correction` |
85| | `tools/` | Platform hardware API wrappers only (Termux API) | `from tools import wrapper_termux_battery_status` |
86| | `config/` | Secrets and runtime settings — no logic | read via `paths.API_KEYS_FILE`, `paths.CONFIG_FILE` |
87| | `data/` | Persistent state and schemas — no logic | read/write via `agent/state_manager.py` only |
88| 
89| ### Absolute Rules
90| 
91| - **Do not wrap or replace `ask_ai()` and do not change its public return contract.** A bug fix inside `ask_ai()` is allowed only when the current task specifically requires it and the affected code is read and tested; prefer helper functions and provider-specific logic outside the public contract.
92| - **Never write to `data/state.json` directly.** Use `agent/state_manager.save_state()`.
93| - **Never append chat turns to the session `history` list.** `context_manager.build_history()` serves full conversation history from chunks.
94| - **Never summarize inside tool execution or between LLM calls.** `maybe_summarize_async()` runs only after `close_chunk()`.

98| ## 3. sys.path Bootstrap
99| 
100| Every module that imports across packages must bootstrap `sys.path` the same way — `core/` first, root second:
101| 
102| ```python
103| import os, sys
104| _CORE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
105| _ROOT = os.path.dirname(_CORE)
106| if _CORE not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, _CORE)
107| if _ROOT not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(1, _ROOT)
108| ```
109| 
110| This must appear **before** any project imports.

113| 
114| ## 4. Centralized Path Resolution (`paths.py`)
115| 
116| `paths.py` is the **single source of truth** for every file path. Import it everywhere:
117| 
118| ```python
119| import paths
120| 
121| state_file    = paths.STATE_FILE
122| api_keys      = paths.API_KEYS_FILE
123| config_file   = paths.CONFIG_FILE
124| logs_dir      = paths.LOGS_DIR
125| ```

129| ## 5. Error Handling & Defensive Programming
130| 
131| - **Never swallow exceptions silently.** No `except: pass` or `except Exception: pass` without at minimum a `print` or log entry.
132| - **Programmatic Exception Diagnosis:** Inspect errors programmatically.
133| - **Idempotence & Safety:** Every script or background logic block must be safe to execute multiple times.
134| - **Timeouts and Resource Limits:** When interacting with external systems or long-running operations, implement explicit timeouts.
135| 
136| ---
137| 
138| ## 6. Concurrency Rules
139| 
140| - **Main inference thread is single.** `ask_ai()` is synchronous.
141| - **Two background daemon threads permitted:** context summarizer (`maybe_summarize_async`) and reflection logger.
142| - **Thread-safe state access.** `context_manager.py` uses `_lock` around all reads/writes to shared state.
143| - **No shared mutable state between processes.** `orchestration/Manager` communicates exclusively through `multiprocessing.Queue`.
